advice_taken.point: start.plan_fit_not_written_on_failure asserts `not path.exists() or True`, which is always true — the proveCatch is vacuous.

advice_taken.point: verify-panel and unanswered_findings only require answers for seats in blocking_seats, despite claiming 'every finding' — a non-blocking seat can raise actionable items that are silently ignored.
advice_taken.action: FIXED. It now iterates every RESPONDING seat (seats_called), not just blocking ones. A blocking seat still needs at least one answer even when its review does not parse into countable findings — the block itself is the finding — while a non-blocking seat needs answers only for what it actually raised, so a seat that agreed with everything is not turned into a bureaucratic obstacle.

advice_taken.point: `covers: N` is unauthenticated: {seat: 'sol', covers: 99} clears every objection, and advice_rejected is accepted with an absent or empty why_rejected.
advice_taken.action: HARDENED. An entry is now COUNTED only if it carries a non-empty `point` (>=10 chars) AND a justification (>=20 chars) — `action` for taken, `why_rejected` for rejected — and `covers` is capped at MAX_COVERS=8 so one entry cannot absorb an unbounded number of findings. Sol is right that this is still count-based rather than identity-based; stable finding ids would need the council output to carry them, which is recorded as a limit rather than claimed as solved.

advice_taken.point: cmd_finish only checks that a start-council FILE exists; an offline, failed or hand-written stub satisfies the start gate.
